records.words: Back to the hill. Last time I could not picture the safe room. The title now mentions people asking to talk about rest; that is what I would want, but those boxes are for new hills, so I will just resume.
Slow straight away this time; last visit a day went while I read.
On the wide screen the cellar is finally big enough to see, with the jars and someone by a fire. This time I am going straight down, deeper, instead of guessing at doors.
Tamar checking the route in daylight is a nice small touch. Marking the stone right under the cellar floor.
The same answer as last time: dig deeper, or shut doors. I am going to open More before I add squares blindly.

Oh. Riders search 9 passage steps from each opening; count steps, not depth. That is the sentence I needed last time and never found. And it paused for reading. Now I can actually plan: a passage that winds more than nine steps, with beds at the end. That feels like a puzzle I can read.
One more square down, then I will turn the passage sideways.
I like that it lists each reachable square. Turning right now.
Three places are beyond riders reach! First time this hill has said anything is safe. Six people, so one more square should do it.
Six places are beyond riders reach. That is exactly six people. I could have cried a little last time for that sentence.

This note is a little late, just after a wait returned at sixty-five seconds. I chose Slow at once, chalked below the cellar, and opened More in the reading. It told me riders search nine passage steps from each opening. I marked a passage down and then right until it said six places are beyond riders reach, for six people. On the wide screen I can see the whole cellar. Now I am waiting for someone to choose to dig; Yusuf says some stone may still be loose.
Meryem coughing dust again. And storage is asking for attention, like last time. I want to see how far the passage has gone first.

Now I can see it: my dashed plan is still there this time, an L of pickaxe squares, and the last two at the far end are shaded grey. I am guessing grey means the safe part. Someone is already standing in the first dug square. I will leave storage for a moment; I want this passage to exist.

Kian still needs to care for his sister Ada. That small line makes him a person. The storage request has stayed, so I will look at furnish; last time it felt like a distraction, but jars matter for the same six people.
Water dry again, same moment as last time. First the store in the cellar corner.
Store marked. It says tap here for water, so I will.
So water is not mine to fix; people choose when to fetch it. Nobody is digging right now either. I can only wait and trust them, which is fine if I can see it moving.
I finally have a plan I understand, and now the game told me plainly why digging stopped: no daylight down there, so I need a lamp. That is a readable consequence, like a puzzle piece.
Hanging the lamp in the dug square at the top of my passage, right above the next chalk.
The lamp got a tick. The log is now mostly the same five people repeated five and six times. I want to see whether the passage grew.
The downward part is dug, three squares, and the store has jars. The sideways chalk is next to the dark bottom, so I am hanging a second lamp there before they stop again.
Requested phone check, not my own choice. Nothing new for two days in the log; I was going to look at the hill anyway.
On the phone the hill is just blank stone with the cellar corner pushed off the top right; my passage is out of view. That is what I fought last time. Back to the wide screen.
Two lamps, the sideways chalk untouched, and nobody in the hill at all for three game days. The view also jumped after the resize. The log is only repeats. Is anyone going to dig it?
Nobody is digging it now. People may choose another task or rest. That tells me what, not why. I will look at the people themselves.
Everyone has a reason: Yusuf discussing marks, Meryem labelling a route, Tariq resting. Nobody is choosing my chalk. I want to see if I can ask Meryem.
I can invite her, which I like, but she has labelled that same visible route seven times. End optional work sounds like it might free her for the chalk. I am guessing.
Nothing visibly changed after End optional work. Same text. Time is paused, so maybe it happens when I close. I will close and watch.

I thought Close would close everything, but it only stepped back to the village list, and time stayed paused the whole wait. Meryem still labels the same route. I liked learning the rule; now I am stuck between a good plan and people who will not dig it.

Oh no. Meryem agrees to stop optional work on the refuge. I thought End optional work would end her route labelling and free her for the chalk. Instead I told the one person I like to stop working on the shelter. It did answer me, at least, and she agreed, but the opposite of what I meant.
Meryem is resting in the shade now. I want to see whether I can take back what I asked.
No way to take it back; End optional work is just greyed. Maybe the words underneath say something.
I need a break from all this. So she did want it. That softens my mistake a lot; maybe I accidentally listened to her. I still need someone to dig. Yusuf is the dig-master; I will look at him.
He keeps saying some stone may still be loose. The line where work must stop today sounds like the thing nobody has told me. I will ask him.
Pending, waits for a quiet moment. Fair. But he has been discussing the same marks for nine entries; I wonder when a quiet moment comes.

Yusuf answered! He showed a crossed-out passage and admitted he once kept people working past the agreed time; a mark must show others when they can stop me. That is a real person with a past, and it was my question that opened it. But the injured worker? I do not know who that is. And a family with a donkey went away because there were no beds. That stung.
Three more game days, still nobody on my sideways chalk. Yusuf keeps saying some stone may still be loose. I am using look on the first undug square to see if that is the reason.
Look gave me no reading at all. Water is dry again. I need to see where things are.
The view has slid on its own; now my chalk is at the very bottom edge, which is why look missed it. I am fitting the hill.

I know exactly what I want: two more squares dug and six beds. The hill even agrees six places would be safe. But for six game days nobody has touched them, the lamp is hung, and every reading just says people may choose another task or rest. The log is the same six lines repeated twelve times. I would close it here. I will give it one more stretch on Steady to see if waiting is all it needs.
Switching to Steady because I am only waiting now, not reading.

Steady only made the same lines repeat faster: thirteen times now. Water still dry, my chalk still untouched. Yusuf’s confession was the best thing tonight, and it is already sinking under the repeats.
Smoke, more than a field fire. This is real, so ringing is not a false alarm. My heart actually jumped. Four are below already, two above. Ringing.
Back to Slow; I want to watch who comes down, not miss it.

Scouts, not an attack. And the report goes person by person: Tamar sleeping three levels down, Kian and Meryem and Yusuf sleeping above ground, all would have been caught. That is very clear and a little chilling; it is the clearest the hill has ever been with me. They searched my passage six levels down too. They may return with more riders, and my two safe squares are still chalk. I rang the bell and they slept anyway.

Kian: I am asleep. That made me laugh, as an answer to an alarm bell. We lived through the first visit, with a tick. But next time they may strike, and my safe room is still two chalk squares nobody will dig. I think this is where I would stop for tonight.
There is an I am stopping choice this time. Selecting it locally. I will not type anything or press Submit.

I am stopping on the evening of 2 September, after the riders scouts left. This visit I finally found the rule I missed last time, nine passage steps, and planned a passage the game agreed would give six safe places. That felt wonderful. Then for most of two weeks nobody dug the last squares, even with lamps, and every reading just said people may choose another task. I accidentally told Meryem to stop work on the refuge, though she did want a break. Yusuf telling me about the crossed-out passage, and Kian saying I am asleep to the bell, were the best moments. I would not leave it running unattended. I would come back another evening if I could understand why people are not digging my marks, because the plan itself is now a puzzle I care about. I am stopping is selected locally; I typed nothing and pressed no Submit.
